Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will cause people to hear the majesty of his voice]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **majesty**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the majestic sound of]

Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh’s **arm** as if it were a person that **descends** to strike in judgment. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will show the downward strike of his arm]
Here, **his arm** represents “his strength.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [his strength]

Isaiah is using **wrath of nose** as a common expression to mean “fierce anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in fierce anger]

Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh’s judgment as if it were a **flame of devouring fire** that consumes everything. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and fire that destroys everything]

31.note: Isaiah is speaking of Yahweh’s judgment on Assyria as if he would **strike them with a rod**, an instrument of punishment. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will punish them]

Here, **the voice of Yahweh** represents “Yahweh’s command and power.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [at Yahweh’s command and power]

The expression **Assyria will be dismayed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The voice of Yahweh will terrify the Assyrians]

32.q: כֹּ֤ל מַֽעֲבַר֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מֽוּסָדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ עָלָ֔י⁠ו
32.note: Isaiah is speaking of each act of Yahweh’s judgment on Assyria as if it were **a stroke of the appointed staff** that Yahweh lays on him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [every act of punishment that Yahweh inflicts on him]

The expression **appointed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the staff he has appointed]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe **battles** that are characterized by **brandishing** weapons. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and in battles with brandished weapons]

33.note: **Tophteh** is a variant spelling of “Topheth,” a name that occurs in several other places in the Bible. Decide as a team, for this instance and for similar ones, whether to use the same name for a given place in each instance where it appears or to use the name that the biblical author does, even if that is a variant. Alternate translation: [Topheth]

As 2 Kings 23:10 indicates, **Tophteh** (or Topheth) was a place within the Valley of Hinnom, where the people of Jerusalem burned their garbage. You could provide this information in a footnote if that would be helpful to your readers.

The expression **Topheth has been arrayed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has arrayed Topheth]

The expression **it has been prepared** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has prepared it for the king]

The pronoun **it** is repeated for emphasis, referring to Topheth, the place of burning. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for indeed, Topheth itself has been prepared]

Isaiah assumes that his readers will understand that it was expected that a king’s body would receive a royal burial in a royal tomb, not shamed by being burned in a fire. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [it has been prepared shamefully for the king]
The pronoun **He** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has deepened, Yahweh has widened]

Isaiah is speaking of **the breath of Yahweh** as if it were a living thing that could kindle a fire. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh himself]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a torrent of brimstone** burns intensely and destructively, so will Yahweh’s breath kindle the fire of judgment. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [burning intensely and destructively]
